title: Scope-lock trigger matrix and comms runway for API / Console / Runtime launch train
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Create an operational protocol that defines the timing and hard triggers for scope freeze across API, Console, and Runtime; and a two-week communications runway and release-notes coordination plan for product, developer docs, and marketing. Scope: milestone signal definitions, scope-lock trigger matrix (autonomy vs blocker rules), release-note owners+templates, cross-team comms cadence, and contingency/rollback thresholds. Out of scope: detailed engineering rollout scripts (ENG to own), marketing creative assets (GTM to own once notes finalized).
acceptance_criteria: A single consolidated scope-lock matrix with deterministic triggers for 'feature hold', 'non-blocking acceptance', and 'rollback' published to Confluence
Clear owners assigned for each release-note section (API, Console, Runtime, Changelogs, Breaking Changes) and one PR template created
Two-week comms calendar (internal and external) with owners and approval gates embedded in the release train calendar
Cross-team readiness signals defined and measurable (SLOs, blocker count, top-3 regression tests passing) and a decision ladder for go/no-go decisions
Fallback plan documented: model variant fallback, canary window sizing, and rollback thresholds tied to error budget burn rate

risks_mitigation: Risk: Last-minute schema change from upstream model onboarding could force cut. Mitigation: require model providers to certify schema compatibility 7 days before GA; keep a compatible minor-version runtime build as fallback. Risk: high error budget burn during canary. Mitigation: limit canary to 5% traffic initially, automatic rollback trigger at 30% error budget burn in 1 hour, and pre-warmed fallback model variant.
